blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — A year after the devastating magnitude 6.9 earthquake jolted northern Cebu on September 30, Bogo City no longer looks like a place in the immediate aftermath of a disaster. Along its streets, people have returned to work, and businesses have reopened. Children are back in school. Roads and public facilities are being repaired, while government services continue from makeshift or newly established spaces. But across the city, traces of destruction from that fateful evening remain. This is Bogo one year later: a city that has moved beyond the emergency phase and is now rebuilding, but one that […]...
